title: alpha-Asarone attenuates synaptic loss in APP/PS1 mice by restoring microglial phagocytic-lysosomal balance via the SPP1-mTOR-TFEB axis.
authors: Jiang, Haitao; Fan, Longmin; He, Jiancong; Zhang, Zheyu
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究alpha-Asarone通过SPP1-mTOR-TFEB轴调节小胶质细胞吞噬-溶酶体功能改善AD突触损伤，虽含分子对接与MD模拟，但核心是细胞/动物药理机制，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Synaptic loss in Alzheimer disease (AD) is closely linked to aberrant microglial phagocytosis. Complement-dependent synaptic pruning and microglial lysosomal dysfunction drive this process, yet effective pharmacological strategies targeting this axis are lacking. alpha-Asarone (ASA) is neuroprotective, but its effects on SPP1-centered microglial synaptic pathology remain unclear. PURPOSE: To determine whether ASA protects against AD-related synaptic injury by modulating SPP1-associated microglial phagocytic-lysosomal dysfunction and define the underlying mechanism. STUDY DESIGN: An integrated in vivo and in vitro pharmacological study was performed using APP/PS1 mice and BV2 microglia. METHODS: Six-month-old APP/PS1 mice were treated with ASA for 100 days and evaluated behaviorally. ASA effects on microglial complement activation, complement-tagged synapses, lysosomal dysfunction, and hippocampal synaptic injury were assessed by transcriptomic analysis, qPCR, western blotting, immunofluorescence, Golgi staining, and transmission electron microscopy. In Abeta-stimulated BV2 cells, the role of SPP1 in phagocytic-lysosomal dysfunction was evaluated using SPP1 knockdown and recombinant SPP1, together with assays of lysosomal acidification, DQ-BSA degradation, and TFEB subcellular localization. Potential ASA-SPP1 engagement was further assessed by molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and cellular thermal shift assay. RESULTS: ASA improved behavioral performance and preserved hippocampal synaptic integrity in APP/PS1 mice. It reduced complement-associated microglial activation, CR3 signal, and complement deposition on PSD95-positive synapses, while restoring lysosomal acidification and proteolysis. SPP1 was upregulated in APP/PS1 mice and suppressed by ASA. ASA also inhibited SPP1-associated mTOR activation, reduced TFEB Ser211 phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention, and improved lysosomal function. SPP1 silencing or mTOR inhibition mimicked ASA, whereas rSPP1 or mTOR activation attenuated these effects. CONCLUSION: ASA attenuated AD-related synaptic injury by restoring microglial phagocytic-lysosomal balance through the SPP1-mTOR-TFEB pathway, supporting its potential as a phytomedicine candidate for AD intervention.
abstract_zh: 背景：阿尔茨海默病（AD）中的突触丢失与异常的小胶质细胞吞噬作用密切相关。补体依赖性突触修剪和小胶质细胞溶酶体功能障碍驱动了这一过程，然而针对该轴的有效药理学策略仍然缺乏。α-细辛脑（ASA）具有神经保护作用，但其对以SPP1为中心的小胶质细胞突触病理的影响尚不清楚。目的：确定ASA是否通过调节SPP1相关的小胶质细胞吞噬-溶酶体功能障碍来保护AD相关的突触损伤，并阐明其潜在机制。研究设计：使用APP/PS1小鼠和BV2小胶质细胞进行了整合的体内和体外药理学研究。方法：对6月龄APP/PS1小鼠给予ASA治疗100天，并进行行为学评估。通过转录组学分析、qPCR、western blotting、免疫荧光、高尔基染色和透射电子显微镜评估ASA对小胶质细胞补体激活、补体标记突触、溶酶体功能障碍和海马突触损伤的影响。在Aβ刺激的BV2细胞中，使用SPP1敲低和重组SPP1，结合溶酶体酸化、DQ-BSA降解和TFEB亚细胞定位的检测，评估SPP1在吞噬-溶酶体功能障碍中的作用。通过分子对接、分子动力学模拟和细胞热位移实验进一步评估ASA与SPP1的潜在结合。结果：ASA改善了APP/PS1小鼠的行为表现并保持了海马突触完整性。它减少了补体相关的小胶质细胞激活、CR3信号和PSD95阳性突触上的补体沉积，同时恢复了溶酶体酸化和蛋白水解。SPP1在APP/PS1小鼠中上调，并被ASA抑制。ASA还抑制了SPP1相关的mTOR激活，减少了TFEB Ser211磷酸化和细胞质滞留，并改善了溶酶体功能。SPP1沉默或mTOR抑制模拟了ASA的效果，而rSPP1或mTOR激活则减弱了这些效应。结论：ASA通过SPP1-mTOR-TFEB通路恢复小胶质细胞吞噬-溶酶体平衡，从而减轻AD相关的突触损伤，支持其作为AD干预植物药候选物的潜力。
